always_load_query=False.description:
Create a semantic dataset from a database table (sql_table), a SQL query (sql), or a SLayer query (query: the dataset becomes query-backed and its fields come from the result).

Host a field or metric on the dataset whose row grain is 1:1 with what it describes, not merely one where its inputs live. Choose relationship keys by field Description (author intent); on ties take the shortest declared relationship path (long chains through lookup or log tables fan out rows). Define entities in dependency order and reference already-defined ones by name; in row-level SQL parenthesise weighted sums in comparisons ((a*w1 + b*w2) > t).

Example: create_dataset(name="orders", sql_table="public.orders", data_source="mydb", fields=[{"name": "amount", "sql": "amount", "datatype": "Float"}], metrics=[{"name": "aov", "expression": "sum(amount) / count(*)"}])

A custom aggregation named sum_sq is called like a built-in: sum_sq(field). Authoring guide: inspect(reference="memory:help.datasets", entity_type="memory").

always_load_query=False.name: ingest_datasource

always_load_query=False.description:
Inspect one entity by reference and kind, a batch when `reference` is a list, or a whole collection when `reference` is omitted. A point lookup: use `search` to find entities by meaning, with related memories.

Before using a field as a filter, projection, group-by or relationship key, inspect it with compact=false and read its Description (the author's intent) and Sample values (stored literal forms; a top-N sample). Build text conditions from these, never from a guessed spelling, and never pick a field by its name alone.

Collection: omit `reference` with entity_type "dataset" (every dataset, grouped by datasource) or "datasource".
Batch: a list of same-kind references returns one block per id in input order (a JSON array in json); a bad id does not sink the batch.
Help: reference "memory:help.intro" (entity_type "memory") for the overview; batch several help topics in one call.

dimensions.description: Group-by fields, one result row per distinct combination: fields named by their dataset (orders.status), a route from it (customers.regions.name), row-level expressions, or {"field": ..., "alias": ...}. date_trunc('<unit>', expr) buckets a timestamp like a time_dimensions entry: date_trunc('month', orders.created_at); units are second, minute, hour, day, week, week_sunday, month, quarter, year, or the datasource's custom ones, while month(orders.created_at) is the month of year (an integer). An aggregate inside a computed dimension needs partition_by= to fix its grain: {"field": "iif(sum(orders.amount, partition_by=customers.id) > 150, 'high', 'low')", "alias": "spend_band"}. Group by naturally readable labels: a name (customers.regions.name), never by an id alone unless ids are asked for; when a name may repeat (people, products), by the id and the name.
dimensions.title: Dimensions

distinct_dimension_values.description: Default true: dimension-only queries return distinct dimension combinations (GROUP BY the projected dimensions). Set false for raw per-record rows — requires empty `metrics` and no metric reference in `filter`/`order`. For rows plus a count, keep the default and add `count(<dataset>.*)`.
distinct_dimension_values.title: Distinct Dimension Values

extensions.description: Query-scoped metrics and relationships added to any dataset this query object reads (its population, a joined dataset, or a stage), at most one entry per dataset, visible only in this query object. A relationship repeating a stored relationship, in either direction, is that edge, and its name is a local alias. An `inner` relationship keeps only the rows with a match; it never multiplies rows. Rooted at orders: [{"dataset": "customers", "metrics": [{"name": "credit_total", "expression": "sum(credit)"}], "relationships": [{"to": "vip_list", "from_columns": ["id"], "to_columns": ["customer_id"], "join_type": "inner"}]}] adds customers.credit_total and keeps only the orders of customers on the vip list.
extensions.title: Extensions

filter.description:
A condition, or a list of conditions AND-ed; each routes automatically to row filtering (WHERE), aggregate filtering (HAVING) or filtering after transforms. SQL operators: = <> < <= > >=, in, between, like / ilike, is null / is not null, IS [NOT] TRUE / FALSE (NULL counts as not true), IS DISTINCT FROM / IS NOT DISTINCT FROM (NULL-safe =), and / or / not, CAST(x AS DATE), regex x ~ '^A[0-9]{3}', JSON payload ->> 'key'; strings are single-quoted ('paid'); build them from the field's sampled values.
- Aggregates and transforms filter too, by expression or by a metric's name: sum(orders.amount) > 100; top N per group: rank(sum(orders.amount), partition_by=customers.regions.name, direction='desc') <= 1.
- Anti-join: rooted at customers, orders.id is null keeps the customers without orders.
- A list tags: contains(tags, 'x') or tags.value = 'x'; contains_any(tags, ['x', 'y']) shares an element, contains_all(tags, ['x', 'y']) holds every one.
- Time points: a string compared with a date/time field is a half-open period: '2025', '2025-Q1', '2025-03', '2025-W05' (ISO week), or relative: 'today', 'last month', 'last 7 days' (excludes the current day), 'year to date'. order_date >= '2025-Q1' starts at the period, <= ends with it, order_date in '2025-Q1' is inside it. A date '2025-03-01' is its midnight; created_at in '2025-03-01' is the whole day.
- {variable} placeholders take literal values from variables.
More: inspect(reference=["memory:help.time", "memory:help.relationships"], entity_type="memory").
filter.title: Filter

limit.description: Max rows to return: the top N, or a limit covering a list longer than the 20 rows an uncapped MCP response returns (with a notice). Never use it to cut a list asked for in full.
limit.title: Limit

main_time_dimension.description: Name (or field) of the time dimension that time-ordered transforms (change, lag, ...) key off; overrides auto-detection when the query has multiple time dimensions.
main_time_dimension.title: Main Time Dimension

metrics.description:
Values to return: expression strings or {"metric": ..., "alias": ...} (alias sets the result key). Every field, metric and row count names its dataset first: orders.amount, orders.revenue (a saved metric), count(orders.*); a bare name is an alias of this query, else a model-scoped metric of a semantic model. AGG(orders.revenue) evaluates the dataset metric. The engine joins the datasets. Expressions combine aggregations with arithmetic, also across datasets: rooted at customers, sum(orders.amount) / count(customers.*) divides the orders' total by the number of customers.
- Aggregations: count(orders.*), sum(orders.amount), count_distinct(orders.customer_id), avg(orders.amount - orders.cost), percentile(orders.amount, p=0.9).
- agg(x) FILTER (WHERE c) aggregates only the rows where c holds: count(orders.*) FILTER (WHERE orders.status = 'paid').
- partition_by= computes an aggregate at a coarser grain, repeated on every row; spell its keys exactly like the query's dimensions. Share of group: sum(orders.amount) / sum(orders.amount, partition_by=customers.regions.name); share of the grand total: sum(orders.amount) / sum(orders.amount, partition_by=[]).
- window= turns any aggregation into a trailing time window ending at each time bucket, in compact durations only ('90d', '3m', '1y'; never '3 months'): count_distinct(orders.customer_id, window='90d').
- Nesting aggregates per-group values: avg(sum(orders.amount, partition_by=[customers.regions.name, customers.id]), partition_by=[customers.regions.name]) averages the per-customer totals in each region.
- Transforms wrap an aggregate; all but the rank family need a time dimension: cumsum(sum(orders.amount)) running total; change(sum(orders.amount)) / change_pct(sum(orders.amount)) period-over-period delta / ratio; time_shift(sum(orders.amount), -1) the previous bucket's value ('year' as a third argument for year-over-year); lag(x, n) / lead(x, n) n rows back / ahead; rank(x, direction='desc') / dense_rank(x, direction='asc') with direction required and partition_by= to rank within groups; ntile(x, n=4) buckets, lowest first; consecutive_periods(sum(orders.amount) > 0) trailing run length.
- A joined dataset's aggregate such as sum(customers.credit) from orders is computed over that dataset's own rows, each customer once. Sliced by a dimension it cannot be attributed to (an order's status), each group aggregates the distinct customers reaching it, with an associated warning (groups may overlap); sum(customers.credit, partition_by=[]) repeats the total on every group instead. Rooted at customers, sum(orders.amount) and sum(returns.amount) in one query are each computed over their own rows: several child datasets never fan out or double count. A child row without a parent (an order with no customer) has NULL parent fields: it counts in the NULL row of a parent dimension when that row exists, and in an ungrouped total; never add it again. An aggregate over a dataset no relationship path reaches from the root is computed over that dataset's own rows and repeated on every row (per bucket of a time_spine time dimension), with an unrelated_dataset warning: rooted at customers, count(events.id) / count(customers.*).
More (every aggregation, empty-input values, nesting and transform rules): inspect(reference=["memory:help.aggregations", "memory:help.transforms"], entity_type="memory").
metrics.title: Metrics

name.description: Stage name. In a list of query objects every entry but the last carries a name, and later stages use it as their population. A STAGE IS NOT NEEDED for top N per group (filter on `rank(...)` in the same stage), for averaging or bucketing per-entity totals (a nested aggregate, or a computed dimension with `partition_by`), or for shares and totals (`partition_by`). A filter on a transform's value (`rank(...) <= 3`, `cumsum(...) > 100`) applies after it, which is computed over every row the other filters keep. Stages ARE needed only to drop rows by a dimension or time condition that a cross-row value must still see, or to join or reuse a whole result: a row filter or date_range applies before a running total, lag / lead, rank, ntile, consecutive_periods or `partition_by` total (change, change_pct, time_shift and window= still read past date_range or a filter on their own time dimension, but not past other filters). Compute the value in an inner stage and filter in the outer one. An outer stage sees the inner result's columns with dotted paths flattened to __: an inner dimension customers.regions.name is customers__regions__name outside; a metric keeps its name. More: inspect(reference=["memory:help.queries"], entity_type="memory").
name.title: Name

order.description: Sort keys, [{"field": ..., "direction": "asc" | "desc", "nulls": "first" | "last"}] (nulls optional). field is a result column name or any aggregate or transform expression, displayed or not: with metrics ["count(orders.*)"], [{"field": "sum(orders.amount)", "direction": "desc"}] sorts by an amount it does not return. Add limit for the top N. Return only the columns the question asks for: never add the sort value to metrics just to sort by it.
order.title: Order

population.description: The population: the rows the result lists. When the question asks for every X (each region, zero included), root at X so rows without facts appear: rooted at regions, the metrics count(customers.orders.id) and {"metric": "sum(iif(customers.orders.order_date >= '2025-01-01', 1, 0))", "alias": "orders_2025"} list every region, including those without orders (a count over no rows is 0, any other aggregate NULL). Always alias a conditional aggregate. Otherwise root where the facts are (rows without facts then drop out), or omit to infer the rows: every dimension combination some metric's rows reach (the dimension values alone with no metrics, one row with no dimensions), reported in the response. A saved dataset or stage name. Write a per-query field as an expression in the position that uses it (a dimension, a filter, an aggregation's argument).
population.title: Population

population_inferred.description: Set by saving; keeps the rows inferred while `population` pins the anchor.
population_inferred.title: Population Inferred

time_dimensions.description: Time-bucketed group-bys — one result row per bucket. Each entry is a TimeDimension dict or the string date_trunc('<unit>', expr), e.g. "date_trunc('month', orders.created_at)"; the field may be any date or time expression, with an optional alias. Buckets without rows are absent. filter.description:
A condition, or a list of conditions AND-ed; each routes automatically to row filtering (WHERE), aggregate filtering (HAVING) or filtering after transforms. SQL operators: = <> < <= > >=, in, between, like / ilike, is null / is not null, IS [NOT] TRUE / FALSE (NULL counts as not true), IS DISTINCT FROM / IS NOT DISTINCT FROM (NULL-safe =), and / or / not, CAST(x AS DATE), regex x ~ '^A[0-9]{3}', JSON payload ->> 'key'; strings are single-quoted ('paid'); build them from the field's sampled values.
- Aggregates and transforms filter too, by expression or by a metric's name: sum(orders.amount) > 100; top N per group: rank(sum(orders.amount), partition_by=customers.regions.name, direction='desc') <= 1.
- Anti-join: rooted at customers, orders.id is null keeps the customers without orders.
- A list tags: contains(tags, 'x') or tags.value = 'x'; contains_any(tags, ['x', 'y']) shares an element, contains_all(tags, ['x', 'y']) holds every one.
- Time points: a string compared with a date/time field is a half-open period: '2025', '2025-Q1', '2025-03', '2025-W05' (ISO week), or relative: 'today', 'last month', 'last 7 days' (excludes the current day), 'year to date'. order_date >= '2025-Q1' starts at the period, <= ends with it, order_date in '2025-Q1' is inside it. A date '2025-03-01' is its midnight; created_at in '2025-03-01' is the whole day.
- {variable} placeholders take literal values from variables.
More: inspect(reference=["memory:help.time", "memory:help.relationships"], entity_type="memory").
filter.title: Filter

limit.description: Max rows to return: the top N, or a limit covering a list longer than the 20 rows an uncapped MCP response returns (with a notice). Never use it to cut a list asked for in full.
limit.title: Limit

main_time_dimension.description: Name (or field) of the time dimension that time-ordered transforms (change, lag, ...) key off; overrides auto-detection when the query has multiple time dimensions.
main_time_dimension.title: Main Time Dimension

metrics.description:
Values to return: expression strings or {"metric": ..., "alias": ...} (alias sets the result key). Every field, metric and row count names its dataset first: orders.amount, orders.revenue (a saved metric), count(orders.*); a bare name is an alias of this query, else a model-scoped metric of a semantic model. AGG(orders.revenue) evaluates the dataset metric. The engine joins the datasets. Expressions combine aggregations with arithmetic, also across datasets: rooted at customers, sum(orders.amount) / count(customers.*) divides the orders' total by the number of customers.
- Aggregations: count(orders.*), sum(orders.amount), count_distinct(orders.customer_id), avg(orders.amount - orders.cost), percentile(orders.amount, p=0.9).
- agg(x) FILTER (WHERE c) aggregates only the rows where c holds: count(orders.*) FILTER (WHERE orders.status = 'paid').
- partition_by= computes an aggregate at a coarser grain, repeated on every row; spell its keys exactly like the query's dimensions. Share of group: sum(orders.amount) / sum(orders.amount, partition_by=customers.regions.name); share of the grand total: sum(orders.amount) / sum(orders.amount, partition_by=[]).
- window= turns any aggregation into a trailing time window ending at each time bucket, in compact durations only ('90d', '3m', '1y'; never '3 months'): count_distinct(orders.customer_id, window='90d').
- Nesting aggregates per-group values: avg(sum(orders.amount, partition_by=[customers.regions.name, customers.id]), partition_by=[customers.regions.name]) averages the per-customer totals in each region.
- Transforms wrap an aggregate; all but the rank family need a time dimension: cumsum(sum(orders.amount)) running total; change(sum(orders.amount)) / change_pct(sum(orders.amount)) period-over-period delta / ratio; time_shift(sum(orders.amount), -1) the previous bucket's value ('year' as a third argument for year-over-year); lag(x, n) / lead(x, n) n rows back / ahead; rank(x, direction='desc') / dense_rank(x, direction='asc') with direction required and partition_by= to rank within groups; ntile(x, n=4) buckets, lowest first; consecutive_periods(sum(orders.amount) > 0) trailing run length.
- A joined dataset's aggregate such as sum(customers.credit) from orders is computed over that dataset's own rows, each customer once. Sliced by a dimension it cannot be attributed to (an order's status), each group aggregates the distinct customers reaching it, with an associated warning (groups may overlap); sum(customers.credit, partition_by=[]) repeats the total on every group instead. Rooted at customers, sum(orders.amount) and sum(returns.amount) in one query are each computed over their own rows: several child datasets never fan out or double count. A child row without a parent (an order with no customer) has NULL parent fields: it counts in the NULL row of a parent dimension when that row exists, and in an ungrouped total; never add it again. An aggregate over a dataset no relationship path reaches from the root is computed over that dataset's own rows and repeated on every row (per bucket of a time_spine time dimension), with an unrelated_dataset warning: rooted at customers, count(events.id) / count(customers.*).
More (every aggregation, empty-input values, nesting and transform rules): inspect(reference=["memory:help.aggregations", "memory:help.transforms"], entity_type="memory").
metrics.title: Metrics

name.description: Stage name. In a list of query objects every entry but the last carries a name, and later stages use it as their population. A STAGE IS NOT NEEDED for top N per group (filter on `rank(...)` in the same stage), for averaging or bucketing per-entity totals (a nested aggregate, or a computed dimension with `partition_by`), or for shares and totals (`partition_by`). A filter on a transform's value (`rank(...) <= 3`, `cumsum(...) > 100`) applies after it, which is computed over every row the other filters keep. Stages ARE needed only to drop rows by a dimension or time condition that a cross-row value must still see, or to join or reuse a whole result: a row filter or date_range applies before a running total, lag / lead, rank, ntile, consecutive_periods or `partition_by` total (change, change_pct, time_shift and window= still read past date_range or a filter on their own time dimension, but not past other filters). Compute the value in an inner stage and filter in the outer one. An outer stage sees the inner result's columns with dotted paths flattened to __: an inner dimension customers.regions.name is customers__regions__name outside; a metric keeps its name. More: inspect(reference=["memory:help.queries"], entity_type="memory").
name.title: Name

order.description: Sort keys, [{"field": ..., "direction": "asc" | "desc", "nulls": "first" | "last"}] (nulls optional). field is a result column name or any aggregate or transform expression, displayed or not: with metrics ["count(orders.*)"], [{"field": "sum(orders.amount)", "direction": "desc"}] sorts by an amount it does not return. Add limit for the top N. Return only the columns the question asks for: never add the sort value to metrics just to sort by it.
order.title: Order

population.description: The population: the rows the result lists. When the question asks for every X (each region, zero included), root at X so rows without facts appear: rooted at regions, the metrics count(customers.orders.id) and {"metric": "sum(iif(customers.orders.order_date >= '2025-01-01', 1, 0))", "alias": "orders_2025"} list every region, including those without orders (a count over no rows is 0, any other aggregate NULL). Always alias a conditional aggregate. Otherwise root where the facts are (rows without facts then drop out), or omit to infer the rows: every dimension combination some metric's rows reach (the dimension values alone with no metrics, one row with no dimensions), reported in the response. A saved dataset or stage name. Write a per-query field as an expression in the position that uses it (a dimension, a filter, an aggregation's argument).
population.title: Population

population_inferred.description: Set by saving; keeps the rows inferred while `population` pins the anchor.
population_inferred.title: Population Inferred

time_dimensions.description: Time-bucketed group-bys — one result row per bucket. Each entry is a TimeDimension dict or the string date_trunc('<unit>', expr), e.g. "date_trunc('month', orders.created_at)"; the field may be any date or time expression, with an optional alias. Buckets without rows are absent. To return every bucket, empty ones included, bucket time_spine.timestamp with a lower date_range bound and aggregate datasets by dotted path: {"field": "time_spine.timestamp", "granularity": "month", "date_range": "2025"} with sum(orders.amount) returns all twelve months. It also lines several datasets up on one time axis.
time_dimensions.title: Time Dimensions

to_many_handling.description: What happens when an aggregation is sliced by a dimension not attributable to it. Omitted (default) or associate: aggregate per cell over the distinct associated rows, e.g. per list element tags.value | error (refuse). To repeat a value across the cells, give the aggregate partition_by= with the dimensions it is attributable to.
to_many_handling.title: To Many Handling

variables.description: {placeholder} values scoped to this query object / stage; the tool-level variables argument overrides. A placeholder binds a literal value only: its text inside quotes ('{s}'), a number, numeric string or boolean in a bare slot, a list as the whole right-hand side of IN (items.status in ({statuses}); over a list field, one list: items.tags in ({wanted})) or as a list literal anywhere else (items.tags = {wanted}, a list-function argument). A placeholder in a name position is an error.
variables.title: Variables

whole_periods_only.description: Snap date filters to whole time buckets and drop the current incomplete bucket.
whole_periods_only.title: Whole Periods Only

SlayerQuery.title: SlayerQuery

alias.description: The result key; defaults to the field's.
alias.title: Alias

date_range.description: The buckets to return: one period ("2025", "2025-Q1", "last month") or [lower, upper] with either bound null (one-sided); a bound may be a {var} placeholder, written unquoted ("{start}"). change, change_pct, time_shift and window= aggregates read rows before the range (a forward time_shift, after it) by themselves, so each month of 2025 with its change vs the previous month is just "2025": never widen the range and drop rows afterwards. cumsum starts at the range start.
date_range.title: Date Range

granularity.description: A built-in granularity, or a custom granularity defined on the query's datasource.
granularity.title: Granularity

conformance.description: "slayer" (default) or "ossie-l3": accept only Ossie Layer 3 queries, refusing others with Ossie's error codes, and name columns by Ossie's output names.
conformance.title: Conformance

dry_run.description: Return the generated SQL without executing it.
dry_run.title: Dry Run

explain.description: Run the database's EXPLAIN and return the query plan.
explain.title: Explain

query.description: A query object, a list of query objects (stages), or a saved query-backed dataset's name.
query.title: Query

refine.description: Saved-dataset-name form only: clauses merged into the saved query's final stage.

show_sql.description: Include the generated SQL in the response.
show_sql.title: Show Sql

variables.description: Values for {placeholder}s in conditions, expressions, date_range bounds and dataset SQL; override a stage's own variables, an outer query's variables and the saved dataset's defaults.
variables.title: Variables

always_load_query=True.name: query

always_load_query=True.description:
Recommend the population (a query's root dataset) for a set of dataset.field / metric items, with each item's reference path from that root, ready to drop into the query (a joined field comes back as customers.regions.name, a root-owned one as status; aggregations are kept).

The root is the dataset from which every item is reachable with the fewest relationship hops. With at least one field item, an aggregated item on a dataset with no relationship path to the root does not block it: its path is flagged unrelated (aggregated over that dataset's own rows). When none reaches everything, population is null and coverage lists the best partial roots for a multi-stage query.

Call it once the item list is final; explore with search / inspect first.

data_source.description: Datasource scope; omitted, names resolve via the datasource priority list.
data_source.title: Data Source

items.description: Entity references: orders.revenue, customers.name, sum(orders.revenue), a saved metric's bare name, ...
items.title: Items

root_hint.description: Intended root (dataset or <data_source>.<dataset>); honoured when it reaches every item, else the automatic pick is used with a warning.
root_hint.title: Root Hint

always_load_query=True.name: recommend_population

always_load_query=True.description:
Save an agent memory: a free-form note plus the SLayer entities it concerns.

With a list of entity references the memory appears among search's memories; with a query object it appears among search's example queries. Returns the memory_id, the canonical entities stored and any warnings. Deleting a dataset, datasource or metric strips references to it from every memory; the note itself is kept.

Examples:
save_memory(learning="orders.is_returned in {0,1,NULL}; treat NULL as not returned", linked_entities=["orders.is_returned"])
save_memory(learning="Paid revenue by status", linked_entities={"population": "orders", "metrics": ["sum(orders.amount)"], "filter": "orders.status = 'paid'"}, id="kb.paid-revenue")

description.description: One-line preview (at most 500 chars) shown by search and compact inspect.
description.title: Description

id.description: Stable memory id such as "kb.policy.42" (no : / ? # or whitespace); an existing id is overwritten. Omit to allocate one.
id.title: Id

linked_entities.description: A list of entity references (resolved to <datasource>.<dataset>[.<leaf>]; memory:<id> links another memory), or a query object whose entities are extracted and which is stored as an example query.
linked_entities.title: Linked Entities

always_load_query=True.name: save_memory

always_load_query=True.description:
Search saved memories, example queries and entities (datasets, fields, metrics, ...) by entity overlap and by meaning.

Call it before `query` to surface notes and example queries saved against the entities you plan to use. Discovery, not detail: hits are one-line descriptions; read the ones you need with `inspect`, batching same-kind ids in one call.

Hits from all channels are fused into one ranked list. With no input it returns the newest memories, with a warning.

compact.description: Default true: one-line hits. False returns full renders; avoid it for broad searches.
compact.title: Compact

cypher_filter.description: openCypher MATCH ... RETURN <node>.id AS id pre-filtering hits to the returned ids, e.g. MATCH (n:DatasetField) RETURN n.id AS id to spend max_results on fields only. Labels: Memory, Datasource, Dataset, DatasetField, Metric, Aggregation; without the advanced_search extra only such label filters work.
cypher_filter.title: Cypher Filter

datasource.description: Restrict every hit to this datasource.
datasource.title: Datasource

entities.description: Entity references; ranks memories tagged with overlapping entities.
entities.title: Entities

query.description: A query object whose entities are extracted and searched like entities.
query.title: Query

question.description: Free text, matched by full text (and by embeddings when configured) over memories and entities.
question.title: Question

always_load_query=True.description: Set how a bare dataset name that exists in several datasources resolves: the first datasource in this list that has it wins; otherwise the name is ambiguous and errors.

priority.description: Existing datasource names, most preferred first; an empty list clears it.
priority.title: Priority

Diff stored datasets against the live database schemas.

Returns, as JSON, the deletes (fields, metrics, relationships, filters, whole datasets) needed to keep the stored datasets valid. Read-only.

data_source.title: Data Source
